study_identification.author_journal_year: Heyuan Jia et al., Communications Medicine, 2025
study_identification.title: Individualized cerebellar damage predicts the presence of behavioral disorders in children with brainstem tumors

study_characteristics.study_objective: To investigate cerebellar damage patterns in children with brainstem tumors and its association with behavioral disorders.

dataset_name.answer: A cohort of 171 pediatric patients from Beijing Tiantan Hospital and 849 healthy children from 4 different sites (72 locally recruited children in Beijing, 69 from the fcon_1000.projects dataset, 450 from the Child Connectome Project (CCNP), and 269 from the Children's Hospital in Guangzhou).

quality_checking_detail.answer: After excluding subjects with severe cerebellar compression or poor image quality, our final analysis included 147 patients and 849 healthy children. Segmentation quality was independently inspected by two neurosurgery specialists. Each specialist conducted their review separately, and manual corrections were performed for inaccurately segmented images based on cerebellar lobule anatomical morphology using ITK-SNAP. Afterward, the two specialists discussed their findings to finalize the most accurate segmentation.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: We utilized the Combat method to harmonize data from different sources, mitigating non-biological variance from inter-scanner discrepancies. This method has been validated for effectively reducing unwanted variation introduced by site differences in structure MRI investigations. Notably, this method retained age, gender, and TIV as covariates while excluding diagnostic labels.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: We initially estimated models with 10-fold cross-validation on the healthy children dataset, then developed definitive models for deviation analysis in patients.

clinical_dataset.answer: A cohort of 171 pediatric patients diagnosed with brainstem tumors at the Department of Neurosurgery, Beijing Tiantan Hospital.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Pearson correlation analysis, ridge regression model with nested five-fold cross-validation (5F-CV), and multiple linear regression models.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Cerebellar damage patterns in patients with brainstem tumors are associated with social problems and withdrawal behavior.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Over 95% of patients are found to have negative deviations in cerebellar regions, particularly in anterior lobules like Left V. Higher tOC is significantly associated with severe social problems (r = 0.31, p = 0.001) and withdrawal behavior (r = 0.28, p = 0.001). Smaller size of cerebellar regions strongly correlates with more pronounced social problems (r = 0.27, p = 0.007) and withdrawal behavior (r = 0.25, p = 0.015).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The normative model included only age and gender. The questionnaire focused mainly on social problems and lacked depth in assessing social functions. The study does not establish causality.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The study introduces a reliable quantitative approach to assess cerebellar damage at the individual level.

general_notes.general_notes: The study used a U-Net-based segmentation algorithm (ACAPULCO) to divide the cerebellum into 26 lobules.
